selected_methods: Tissues were first sectioned to 5 μm in thickness using a microtome. Immunohistochemistry was performed on a Leica Bond Rxm automated IHC/ISH stainer using the Bond Refined Detection kit and antibodies to HIF-1α (1:250; #100066421, Cayman Chemical, Ann Arbor, MI, USA), CAIX (1:500; #NB-100-417, Novus Biologicals, Centennial, CO, USA), and PLOD2 (1:200; #21214-1-AP, Proteintech, Chicago, IL, USA). Nuclei were counterstained with hematoxylin. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded biopsy sections were stained with Masson’s Trichrome according to standard protocols to visualize fibrillar collagen fibers. Stained slides were scanned into digital images using an Aperio VERSA scanner at 20x magnification (Leica Biosystems, Heidelberg, Germany) and analyzed with Aperio ImageScope software (positive pixel count algorithm for all markers). The Aperio ImageScope software was used to objectively and reliably quantify the pixel counts for HIF-1α, CAIX, and PLOD2.

18F-FMISO scans were obtained within 2 weeks of percutaneous biopsies. An intravenous (IV) line was placed for the injection of the radiotracer. A dose of 5–10 mCi (185–370 MBq) of 18F-FMISO was administered. Subjects were imaged in the supine position, approximately 60 min after the injection of the tracer at 3 min per bed. All 18F-FMISO scans were research scans. These scans had to cover the abdomen (to include the liver) and the entire tumor. The transaxial FOV was ~ 70 cm and the axial FOV varied from 15 to 25 cm. A low-dose computed tomography (CT) scan (100–140 kVp, variable mA, 5 mm slice thickness) was acquired for attenuation correction and anatomical localization of findings in the PET scan.

A circular region of interest (ROI) was centered over the biopsied area based on the biopsy tract to include the entire tumor, and the sarcoma maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) was automatically calculated using MIM software (Cleveland, OH, USA). The lesion ROI size was not fixed but based on the extension of the morphological lesion on CT. Another circular ROI was placed over adjacent normal skeletal muscle matched to the site of the STS and the muscle SUVmax was calculated following the method described by Rajendran et al. [16].

18F-FDG PET/CT studies were obtained within 2 weeks of percutaneous biopsies, and at least 24 h before or after the 18F-FMISO PET/CT studies. For the 18F-FDG PET/CT studies that were utilized in this study, subjects had to fast for at least 4 h prior to the study and had to have a blood glucose level less than 200 mg/dl (11.1 mmol/L) prior to the injection of the radiotracer. For clinical studies, the field of view (FOV) was from the skull-base to the mid-thighs. The subject was given approximately 225 ml of dilute oral contrast (approximately 9 g barium sulphate) (Readi-Cat2, Bracco, NJ, USA) approximately 30 min before, and then after the intravenous administration of the radiotracer. Subjects #1 and #2 had research 18F-FDG PET/CTs, Subject #3 had a clinical 18F-FDG PET/CTs, Subject #4 did not have a 18F-FDG PET/CT and Subject #5 had a simulation 18F-FDG PET/CT for radiation treatment planning. The FOV was the whole body (vertex to toes) if it was a clinical/research study (x3) or low abdomen to mid leg for the simulation study. The transaxial FOV was ~ 70 cm and the axial FOV varied from 15 to 25 cm. The FOV size was 50–60 cm to ensure the entire body contour was included for attenuation correction. Subjects were injected with between 8 and 20 mCi (296–740 MBq) of 18F-FDG and imaged in the supine position approximately 60 min after the injection at 3 min per bed. A low-dose CT scan (100–140 kVp, variable mA, 5 mm slice thickness) was also acquired for attenuation correction and anatomical localization of findings in the PET scan. A 512 × 512 reconstruction matrix was utilized.

selected_methods: Prospective samples were collected for the VorteX Biobank from consenting adult patients with localised, extremity soft tissue sarcoma receiving surgery with adjuvant radiotherapy as part of the phase III randomised controlled VorteX trial. The study had appropriate ethical approval (LREC 06/MRE/03/3) and informed consent was obtained for sample collection and analysis. Fresh tumour, matched normal tissue, formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue and peripheral blood samples were collected prior to radiotherapy.

Tumour areas in FFPE material were demarcated by the VorteX trial histopathologist (DH) and 1 mm diameter cores were taken in triplicate from different areas. A maximum of 120 cores were placed within a single FFPE block in a standardised pattern (MTA-1; Beecher Instruments, Silver Spring, MD, USA). Eleven tissue microarrays (TMAs) were prepared in total.

Sections were prepared in duplicate from each TMA for staining for a marker of interest and matched negative control. Positive controls included FFPE sections of hypoxic and normoxic cell pellets and tissue sections from other tumours that had shown high or low expression of the markers in previous experiments (Hunter et al, 2014). Tumour capillary staining was used as an additional internal control for GLUT1 staining.

Slides were viewed using Leica SCN400 Image Viewer and scored at × 8 magnification. The percentage of tumour cells per core expressing each marker was determined. Intensity was recorded for potential future use, but was not used in the current analysis in favour of a simpler scoring system. Negative controls were available for comparison. For HIF-1α only nuclear staining was considered, for CAIX only membrane staining was scored and for GLUT1 membrane and cytoplasmic staining were included.

Cores were scored twice by the same scorer (LF) on different days. For HIF-1α and GLUT1 all cores were also scored by a specialist sarcoma consultant histopathologist (SS) and for CAIX this was done for all cores with staining present (PS). Scorers were blinded to clinical outcomes. The score of the consultant histopathologist was taken if scores were discordant. The final score was an average across all cores for each tumour type. Definitions of marker positivity were selected to reflect those used in previous publications.
